title: WHEN SIN BRINGS ITS OWN CONSEQUENCE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The anger of the Lord burned against them, and he left them. When the cloud lifted from above the tent, Miriam's skin was leprous — it became as white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she had a defiling skin disease, — Num 12:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The cloud lifts, God withdraws, and Miriam is left with a defiling skin disease. This is a hard moment, and we should not rush past it. Her jealousy and slander were not trivial in God's eyes, and here the consequence is visible and severe.

We often treat our critical words as harmless — a little venting, a private complaint. But sin is never as small as it feels in the moment. Miriam's tongue had spread a kind of spiritual disease through the camp, and now that corruption showed on her own body. Under the old covenant, God sometimes made the inward reality outwardly visible, teaching Israel the seriousness of sin.

Notice that it was Miriam who was struck, though Aaron shared the sin. Scripture suggests she was the instigator. Yet Aaron, the priest, could only turn and look — he had no power to heal his sister. Human religion and human effort cannot cleanse the deep defilement of sin.

That is why this points us to Christ. Where Aaron could only look on helplessly, Jesus touched lepers and made them clean. He does not merely observe our defilement from a distance; He takes it upon Himself and heals it. The disease Miriam could not cure, and Aaron could not remove, Christ came to conquer at the cross. What our sin deserves, He bore; what we could never cleanse, He washes white as snow.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take the consequences of your words and attitudes seriously?
2. Where in your life have you tried to fix defilement by your own effort?
3. How does Christ's power to cleanse the leper give you hope today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, teach me to see my sin as You see it, not as a small thing. Thank You that Christ cleanses what I never could. Wash me clean and guard my heart and tongue. Amen.
